rows.concept: Transcript mirror entries are opaque JSON blobs

upstream.behavior: Mirror entries pass through without validation; a malformed entry never fails the frame.

rows.concept: Non-JSON CLI stdout lines

upstream.behavior: Both skip non-JSON lines. Python raises on a line that starts with '{' and does not parse; TypeScript logs and skips every unparseable line.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect and skips every stdout line that does not decode. ArgvStyle::Python skips only the lines that do not start with '{', fails on a corrupt '{' line with JsonDecodeError as CLIJSONDecodeError does, and drops a corrupt unterminated tail at the end of the stream as Python does.

rows.concept: control_response with an unknown request_id

upstream.behavior: An unmatched control_response is not an error; TypeScript buffers up to 1024 for awaitControlResponse, Python drops it.

rows.concept: session_state_changed with an unknown state

upstream.behavior: Any state value is stored; only 'idle' ends the run.

rows.concept: No idle state after the last result

typescript.anchor: ms after the last result, ending the run

upstream.behavior: When the run-end ceiling expires the run ends normally with a debug log, not an error.

rows.concept: Run-end ceiling read from the environment

upstream.behavior: CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS sets the run-end ceiling, 0 for no limit, clamped to 2^31-1 ms, default 600000. TypeScript reads it from the child environment with exponent, grouped-digit and leading-digit spellings; Python reads options.env then os.environ with int().

decision.reason: The default dialect follows TypeScript; Limits::python() selects Python's int() parse and lookup order, and RunEndTimeout::Fixed is an opt-in override.

rows.concept: initialize answered with hooks_applied false

typescript.anchor: does not honor onFailure on hook matchers

upstream.behavior: hooks_applied false is an error only when a hook is set to block on failure.

rows.concept: Repeated MCP initialize on a live SDK server

upstream.behavior: A second initialize is accepted and renegotiates the protocol version.

rows.concept: Requests before notifications/initialized

upstream.behavior: TypeScript does not gate requests on initialization. The Python mcp server refuses every request except ping before initialize with -32602, and initialize alone opens the session.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; McpServerDialect::Python reproduces the Python server.

rows.concept: initialize parameter validation

upstream.behavior: Both check initialize params for presence and type only and accept empty strings. TypeScript answers invalid params with -32603 carrying the zod issues; Python answers -32602 Invalid request parameters.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; McpServerDialect::Python reproduces the Python server.

rows.concept: MCP protocol version negotiation

upstream.behavior: TypeScript echoes 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05 or 2024-10-07; Python echoes the same versions except 2024-10-07. Both answer any other version with 2025-11-25.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; McpServerDialect::Python reproduces the Python server.

rows.concept: SDK MCP tool names outside the naming standard

upstream.behavior: A tool name outside the MCP naming standard is still registered and listed; only TypeScript also logs a warning.

rows.concept: Size of outbound user messages

upstream.behavior: User messages are serialized and written without a size cap.

rows.concept: Number of registered hook callbacks

upstream.behavior: Hook callbacks are registered without a count limit.

rows.concept: tools, allowedTools and disallowedTools argv

upstream.behavior: Tool lists are joined with ',' and passed through without entry validation.

rows.concept: Sending a prompt while a turn is running

upstream.behavior: Prompts are written whenever the caller sends them; the CLI queues them.

rows.concept: interrupt control response shape

upstream.behavior: The interrupt response is never fatal; TypeScript filters non-string entries, Python ignores the body.

rows.concept: Unknown permission modes

upstream.behavior: Permission modes pass through untyped; unknown values are not rejected.

rows.concept: User input content validation

upstream.behavior: User input is written verbatim; the CLI and API validate content.

rows.concept: Transcript mirror pending entry and byte thresholds

upstream.behavior: Exceeding the pending thresholds (500 entries, 1 MiB) triggers an eager flush; nothing is rejected.

rows.concept: Transcript mirror append failure

upstream.behavior: A failed append is reported as a system mirror_error message; the run outcome is unaffected.

rows.concept: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR differs from the session store config directory

python.reason: Python always mirrors from the subprocess config dir and has no custom spawn hook to warn about.

typescript.anchor: ensure the subprocess CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR matches the parent

upstream.behavior: A possible mismatch is at most a warning, never an error.

rows.concept: Resume with a non-UUID session id

upstream.behavior: A non-UUID resume id skips store materialization and leaves --resume to the CLI.

rows.concept: Resume of a session with no stored entries

upstream.behavior: A missing or empty stored session materializes nothing and is not an error.

rows.concept: Unsafe subkeys returned by list_subkeys

upstream.behavior: Unsafe subpaths (empty, absolute, '..', escaping the session dir) are skipped with a warning.

rows.concept: Transcript path to session key

upstream.behavior: Both paths are resolved against the working directory first, so relative paths work; two parts ending in .jsonl give a main key and four or more parts give a subpath key with .jsonl stripped. Nothing is validated. On Windows the paths compare case-insensitively with both separators, drives and UNC shares, and the project, session and subpath names keep the case of the transcript path; Python reads a part with a colon second, such as a:x, as a drive (ntpath.join restarts the path there and PureWindowsPath makes it the first part), so its keys differ from TypeScript's at those parts; SessionKey::from_transcript_path_with takes the SummaryDialect (TypeScript by default, also used by the mirror unless the store options say Python) and the Python dialect reproduces CPython 3.12.16, the oracle the crate follows. The goldens record where CPython 3.13 and later differ as python_since_3_13.

rows.concept: Continue when the newest listed session id is not a UUID

typescript.anchor: Options.continue with sessionStore requires store.listSessions to be implemented

upstream.behavior: Python skips the candidate and tries the next newest. TypeScript takes the newest entry only, so a non-UUID newest id starts a fresh session.

decision.reason: Both rules are exposed through SessionStoreOptions.dialect. TypeScript, the default, takes only the newest listed session and starts fresh when its id is not a UUID; the Python dialect tries the next newest.

rows.concept: Unknown permission suggestion destinations, behaviors and update types

upstream.behavior: Neither SDK validates suggestion values. TypeScript passes permission_suggestions raw to canUseTool; Python accepts any string for type, destination, behavior and mode, so an unrecognized suggestion reaches the callback and round-trips verbatim into updatedPermissions.

rows.concept: Structurally malformed permission suggestions and requests

upstream.behavior: Python decodes every suggestion, so a structurally broken one (a missing type, rules that are not a list) or a missing tool_name raises inside the control handler, which answers that request with an error response while the session continues. TypeScript forwards the raw suggestions to canUseTool without decoding them, so nothing fails.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect and hands every field to the callback as sent, keeping broken suggestions as PermissionUpdate::Unknown; ArgvStyle::Python reproduces claude_agent_sdk's from_dict errors and the order it raises them in.

rows.concept: Which transcript mirror append errors are retried

upstream.behavior: Every non-timeout append error is retried, three attempts with 200 ms and 800 ms backoff.

rows.concept: session_store combined with file checkpointing

typescript.anchor: enableFileCheckpointing is not yet supported with sessionStore

upstream.behavior: Configuring a session store together with file checkpointing is rejected before spawn.

rows.concept: Where store-backed resume transcripts are materialized

upstream.behavior: Transcripts are written to a fresh temp dir that becomes the subprocess CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, on every platform.

rows.concept: Two SDK MCP tools with the same name

upstream.behavior: TypeScript throws 'Tool <name> is already registered'. Python keeps the last handler and lists both tools.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default: SdkTools::new rejects a repeated name with McpServer.registerTool's error. SdkTools::with_duplicates keeps every definition, lists them all and runs the last one with the name, as Python's create_sdk_mcp_server does.

rows.concept: tools/call for an unknown tool

typescript.anchor: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool

upstream.behavior: An unknown tool returns an isError tool result naming the tool, not a JSON-RPC error.

rows.concept: tools/call arguments that fail the input schema

typescript.anchor: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool

upstream.behavior: Invalid arguments return an isError tool result with an input validation message, not a JSON-RPC error.

rows.concept: JSON-RPC request id type

upstream.behavior: Both read a string or an integer id. TypeScript also reads a number with a zero fraction as that integer and drops ids outside the safe integer range; Python reads any other id as a notification and refuses an id already in flight.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; McpServerDialect::Python reproduces the Python server.

rows.concept: Blocking hooks against a responder without onFailure support

typescript.anchor: does not honor onFailure on hook matchers

upstream.behavior: Initialize fails when a blocking hook is configured and hook_on_failure_supported is not true.

rows.concept: Waiting for a control_response

upstream.behavior: Python times out after 60 s with "Control request timeout: {subtype}". TypeScript waits until the response arrives, the abort signal fires, or the query closes; its only initialize deadline is 660000 ms, armed when a hook is set to block on failure or managed settings are sent.

decision.reason: Limits::control_timeout is None by default and InitializeTimeout::TypeScript arms 660 s only for blocking hooks or managed settings, failing with InitializeNotConfirmed or ManagedSettingsNotConfirmed and TypeScript's text. Limits::python() selects the 60 s wait, Python's message and the CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT initialize wait.

rows.concept: control_response with an error subtype

upstream.behavior: An error subtype rejects the pending request with the CLI's error message.

rows.concept: Size of one inbound stdout message

upstream.behavior: Python rejects a line over max_buffer_size (1 MiB by default) with "JSON message exceeded maximum buffer size of {N} bytes". TypeScript reads lines with node:readline and no length limit.

decision.reason: Limits::max_buffer_size is None by default; Limits::python() sets Python's 1 MiB cap with its message.

rows.concept: SessionStore load timeout

upstream.behavior: Store loads time out after 60000 ms by default.

rows.concept: Retrying a timed-out mirror append

upstream.behavior: A timed-out append is not retried because the in-flight call may still land.

rows.concept: Continue when the newest session is a sidechain

typescript.anchor: Options.continue with sessionStore requires store.listSessions to be implemented

upstream.behavior: Python walks newest to oldest and skips sessions whose first entry has isSidechain true. TypeScript resumes the newest listed session.

decision.reason: Both rules are exposed through SessionStoreOptions.dialect. TypeScript, the default, resumes the newest listed session even when it is a sidechain; the Python dialect walks past sidechains.

rows.concept: Project key derivation

upstream.behavior: Non-alphanumerics become '-'; keys over 200 chars are truncated and suffixed with a base36 hash. A project key is never validated upstream, so SessionProjectKey::new takes any name and SessionProjectKey::checked is the opt-in Rust-only check.

rows.concept: Mirror frame whose file path is outside the projects dir

upstream.behavior: The frame is dropped with a warning.

rows.concept: continue with a store lacking list_sessions

typescript.anchor: Options.continue with sessionStore requires store.listSessions to be implemented

upstream.behavior: continue without an explicit resume requires the store to implement list_sessions.

rows.concept: Queue capacity bounds

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: No queue capacity setting exists upstream. Rust queues are unbounded unless a caller opts into a bound, and an opted-in QueueCapacity still rejects zero and values past the semaphore permit limit.

rows.concept: Timeout value bounds

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Timeouts are not range-checked upstream. Timeout::new accepts any duration and a deadline past the clock's range never fires; Timeout::checked keeps the Zero and TooLarge errors for callers that want them.

rows.concept: max budget value

upstream.behavior: The budget is passed to the CLI without validation: TypeScript as --max-budget-usd=${String(f)} and Python as str(value) after --max-budget-usd.

rows.concept: CLI path that is a .bat or .cmd script

typescript.reason: sdk.mjs resolves and spawns the CLI path without a batch-script guard.

upstream.behavior: Python refuses .bat and .cmd CLI paths on Windows. TypeScript spawns them.

decision.reason: WindowsBatchCli::Run is the default, so a .bat or .cmd path starts as in TypeScript; WindowsBatchCli::Refuse selects Python's refusal, which fires only on Windows and quotes the path as Python's repr does, as CliPathError::WindowsBatchScript. Paths and refusal text captured from the real Python package on each platform pin both sides.

rows.concept: Timeout on a stdin write

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Writes to the CLI are not time-bounded upstream; TypeScript only logs when the stdin buffer is full. Rust waits for the write unless Limits::write_timeout is set, which fails a stalled write with WriteTimeout.

rows.concept: Timeout waiting for the client command queue

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: No client command queue exists upstream. Rust's command queue is unbounded and never times out unless Limits::command_queue_capacity is set; Limits::command_queue_timeout then bounds the wait for room with CommandQueueTimeout.

rows.concept: Shutdown and stderr drain timeouts

upstream.behavior: TypeScript closes stdin, waits 2000 ms, sends SIGTERM (none on Windows) and SIGKILL 5000 ms later without waiting, gives stderr 200 ms after the exit, and never reports an error. Python waits 5 s, terminates, waits 5 s, kills and waits 5 s, suppressing every error.

decision.reason: Shutdown::TypeScript is the default; Limits::python() selects Shutdown::Python, and Shutdown::Strict keeps ShutdownTimeout and StderrDrainTimeout as an opt-in.

rows.concept: Retained stderr tail size

upstream.behavior: TypeScript keeps the last 2048 UTF-16 code units of stderr and appends them, trimmed, to the process error. Python keeps no stderr and reports "Check stderr output for details".

decision.reason: Limits::stderr_tail defaults to TypeScript's 2048 units; Limits::python() sets it to 0. The tail grows and is cut as TypeScript's does, and its secrets are redacted in the TypeScript dialect only (see r12-stderr-redaction).

rows.concept: Secret redaction of stderr-derived error text

python.reason: Python keeps no stderr tail and redacts nothing.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript removes secret-shaped tokens (bearer and basic credentials, vendor API keys, cloud and source host tokens, webhooks, JWTs) from the stderr tail, from the spawn failure message and from the path in the not found and failed to launch message. Python puts none of that text in its errors.

decision.reason: The TypeScript dialect redacts with the same eighteen patterns in the same order, run on a matcher with JavaScript semantics; ArgvStyle::Python keeps its tail unredacted.

rows.concept: Control request id exhaustion

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Upstream request ids are random strings that never run out. The Rust counter wraps by default so ids never run out either; RequestIdExhaustion::Fail keeps RequestIdExhausted as an opt-in.

rows.concept: Sending before initialize or after input closed

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Upstream holds writes until initialize is sent and writes input sent after the caller ended its stream. Rust writes such input by default; InputAfterFinish::Reject keeps InputClosed as an opt-in. NotInitialized is only reachable from inside the driver, because the client returns only after initialize succeeds.

rows.concept: Outstanding outbound control requests

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Outstanding control requests are unbounded upstream. Limits::max_pending_controls is opt-in and fails the excess request with TooManyControls.

rows.concept: Outstanding inbound SDK callbacks

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Inbound callbacks are unbounded upstream. Limits::max_incoming_callbacks is opt-in and answers a request that would start one more callback with an error response; requests answered without a callback are not counted.

rows.concept: Deferred message queue capacity

upstream.behavior: TypeScript queues messages in an unbounded array and keeps reading stdout. Python buffers 100 messages and then stops reading until the caller takes one.

decision.reason: MessageBuffer::Unbounded is the default; Limits::python() selects MessageBuffer::Backpressure(100), and MessageBuffer::FailWhenFull keeps MessageQueueFull as an opt-in.

rows.concept: Tracked background tasks

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Tracked tasks are unbounded upstream. Limits::max_tracked_tasks is opt-in and fails the run with TooManyTasks.

rows.concept: Queued turns

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Queued prompts are unbounded upstream. Limits::max_queued_inputs is opt-in and fails with TooManyInputs.

rows.concept: Inbound control_request with a duplicate id

upstream.behavior: TypeScript skips an inbound request whose id is still in flight, with a debug log and no response. Python runs both handlers and both answer.

decision.reason: DuplicateControlRequests::Skip is the default; Limits::python() selects RunBoth, and DuplicateControlRequests::Fail keeps DuplicateControlRequest as an opt-in.

rows.concept: Same MCP server name in SDK and external maps

python.reason: Python keeps one mcp_servers dict, so a name holds one config.

upstream.behavior: In-process servers are spread over the external configs, so an in-process server silently replaces an external config of the same name and keeps its position.

rows.concept: Concurrent MCP server updates

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no set_mcp_servers.

upstream.behavior: setMcpServers is not serialized: in-process servers are swapped before mcp_set_servers is sent, overlapping calls each send their request, and response errors are not reconciled.

rows.concept: External MCP server URL

upstream.behavior: Server configs, URLs included, are serialized to --mcp-config verbatim with no URL check.

rows.concept: SDK MCP tool input schema type

python.reason: Python sends the declared schema through the mcp package Tool model, which is outside the pinned sources.

upstream.behavior: The declared input schema is listed as given. Python's run_tool reports a schema error as the tool result text; neither SDK requires type 'object' before the server starts.

rows.concept: External $ref in output schemas

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Output schemas are passed through upstream.

rows.concept: Extension input block kind and fields

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: No typed extension blocks exist upstream.

rows.concept: Reserved kind field in message origin

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Origins are passed through upstream.

rows.concept: Session key component safety

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: SessionKey::new, SessionProjectKey::new and SessionSubpath::new accept any text, as upstream does. Upstream skips a non-UUID resume id and, with a warning, every listSubkeys subpath its own dialect rejects; Rust applies that dialect's rule at the resume site, and SessionKey::checked, SessionProjectKey::checked and SessionSubpath::checked are the opt-in Rust-only safety checks. The Windows rules of both resume guards run on any host from a platform parameter and are pinned by goldens captured with Node path.win32 and Python ntpath; what Python's resolve() does on a real Windows file system (reserved device names) is not capturable off Windows. The Rust-only extras (empty components, reserved device names) live only in the opt-in SessionSubpath::checked, which reads a drive as the platform does (any character before a colon on Windows, a letter on POSIX; Python's own guard reads any character on every host, pinned by POSIX goldens). The project directory name folds to lowercase on Windows only, through one function both listings use, pinned by a golden captured with Node toLowerCase and Python lower.

rows.concept: Resume entry, byte and subkey limits

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Store loads are unbounded upstream. Rust is unbounded by default; max_resume_entries, max_resume_bytes and max_subkeys opt into EntryLimit, ByteLimit and SubpathLimit.

rows.concept: Exclusive, no-follow transcript writes

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Upstream writes into a fresh private temp dir, so no collision checks are needed.

rows.concept: Config directory presence and path safety

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Upstream creates its own temp config dir and copies auth files from the caller's config dir or home directory (see r31-home-directory-fallback for the home lookup), joining a relative path as given; TypeScript keeps an empty options.env value while Python falls through to the next source. Rust does the same by default; SessionStoreOptions::require_absolute_config_paths opts into UnsafeConfigPath.

rows.concept: Transcript mirror queue full or closed

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: The upstream mirror batcher is not a bounded queue.

rows.concept: Bound on the final mirror flush

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: The final flush is not separately bounded upstream. Rust waits for the flush by default, each append still bounded by append_timeout; SessionStoreLimits::flush_timeout opts into a deadline that fails with MirrorFlushTimeout.

rows.concept: Retained mirror failure records

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no equivalent bound.

upstream.behavior: Upstream keeps no failure records and reports every failed append. Rust reports every failure by default; SessionStoreLimits::max_retained_failures opts into a cap that folds the overflow into one Suppressed failure.

rows.concept: Output that ends in the middle of a turn

upstream.behavior: Both treat only a failed exit as an error: when the CLI exits with status 0 before a result, the messages end quietly after what arrived. Rust ends them the same way by default; EndWithoutResult::Fail keeps UnexpectedEof as an opt-in.

rows.concept: Hook registration without a matcher

upstream.behavior: Python always sends the matcher key and sends null when no matcher is set. TypeScript sends the key as undefined, which JSON serialization drops, so the registration has no matcher key.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect and declares matcher as an optional string, so the key is omitted; ArgvStyle::Python sends null.

rows.concept: User dialog request that no handler answers

upstream.behavior: Python has no user dialog support, so the request reaches its unsupported subtype branch and is answered with an error response. TypeScript with no handler, or a handler that returns null, deliberately sends no response so a capable client can answer.

decision.reason: An answer from this client would pre-empt another client that can show the dialog, and an error would end the dialog for the user, so the default writes nothing and the session continues. ArgvStyle::Python answers with Python's unsupported-subtype error when no handler is registered.

rows.concept: Bundled Claude Code executable beside the Python package

typescript.reason: sdk.mjs resolves a platform package instead of a bundled directory.

upstream.behavior: Python checks <package>/_bundled/claude (claude.exe on Windows) before any other discovery and accepts it only when it exists and is a file. TypeScript has no bundled directory and resolves the native binary from its platform package.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default and has no bundled lookup. ClaudeAgentOptions::bundled_cli_root names the directory that holds _bundled, Python's package directory, and connect then takes the bundled executable before PATH as _find_cli does.

rows.concept: Native executable from the platform optional dependency package

python.reason: The pinned Python sources bundle the binary in the wheel and never resolve npm packages.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript resolves <package>-<platform>-<arch>/claude (claude.exe on win32) through Node module resolution, tries the musl variant first on musl Linux and the glibc one first otherwise, uses a dedicated linux-<arch>-android package for Android, skips a candidate whose resolution throws or whose file is missing, and fails with a message naming the platform when none is found.

rows.concept: Minimum version a bundled Claude Code record must meet to derive an app label

typescript.reason: sdk.mjs has no derived client app minimum and reads no version record.

upstream.behavior: The recorded version must start with major.minor.patch (up to nine digits each) and that triple, compared as a list, must not be below 999.0.0 (DERIVED_CLIENT_APP_MINIMUM_CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION). Nothing qualifies until upstream lowers the minimum.

rows.concept: Bundled Claude Code executable as the trigger for a derived client app label

typescript.reason: sdk.mjs derives no client app label from the executable that it spawns.

upstream.behavior: Python derives a label only when the SDK package pin (__cli_version__) meets the minimum, the spawned CLI is the bundled executable, and the claude.version file beside it records a version that meets the minimum. Any other CLI counts as too old, a bundled one with no readable record does too, and a failure to read never breaks connect. TypeScript derives no label.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default and derives no label. ClaudeAgentOptions::client_app_derivation set to ClientAppDerivation::Bundled(BundledCli) selects Python's trigger for a caller-supplied package root and pin, because a Rust crate has no package directory or __cli_version__, and the label names this crate because Rust has no Python distribution metadata.

rows.concept: Outbound control request id and envelope

upstream.behavior: TypeScript sends Math.random().toString(36).substring(2,15) with no counter, in a compact envelope that starts with request_id. Python sends req_{counter}_{8 hex digits} in an envelope that starts with type, written by json.dumps with spaced separators and ASCII escapes.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; ArgvStyle::Python selects the Python id, envelope order and json.dumps spelling.

rows.concept: Initialize request fields and hook matcher entries

upstream.behavior: TypeScript omits hooks when none are configured, omits an unset matcher, and sends jsonSchema, systemPrompt, appendSystemPrompt and supportedDialogKinds in the request. Python sends hooks null when none are configured, matcher null when unset, and none of those prompt or schema fields. Both skip events with no matchers and keep matchers with no callbacks.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; ArgvStyle::Python sends the Python request.

rows.concept: Initialize response that is not the documented object

upstream.behavior: Neither SDK validates the initialize response. TypeScript keeps any value as the initialization result; Python replaces anything but an object with an empty object.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; ArgvStyle::Python reads a non-object as an empty object. Typed fields of an unexpected type read as absent and the response stays available unchanged.

rows.concept: supportedDialogKinds without onUserDialog

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no user dialog support.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript refuses non-empty dialog kinds without a handler before the session starts.

rows.concept: Initialize response for managed settings and plugins sent in initialize

python.reason: The pinned Python sources do not send managed settings or plugins in initialize.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript ends the session when managed settings were sent and managed_settings_applied is not true, and logs a warning when plugins were sent and plugins_applied is not true.

rows.concept: Messages that are unknown, malformed or missing required keys

upstream.behavior: TypeScript yields every message the CLI writes without validating it, consuming only keep_alive and host-only session_state_changed. Python parse_message raises MessageParseError with a KeyError text for a known message missing a key it reads, skips unknown message types and skips content blocks of kinds it does not parse.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default and never loses a message, so newer CLI shapes still reach the caller. MessageDecoding::Python reproduces parse_message, error texts included, for callers that need Python's outcome.

rows.concept: Where the system prompt travels and which forms it takes

upstream.behavior: TypeScript sends the prompt in the initialize request (systemPrompt as a list, appendSystemPrompt, systemPromptSnapshot, excludeDynamicSections) and has no prompt flag. Python puts the prompt on the command line (--system-prompt, --system-prompt-file, --append-system-prompt) and sends only excludeDynamicSections and systemPromptSnapshot in the request.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect. ArgvStyle::Python selects Python's argv and request, and the prompt forms that exist in only one SDK (a list of texts, a prompt file) are refused in the other dialect instead of being dropped.

rows.concept: workspaceTrust with an accepted trust and no absolute directory

python.reason: claude_agent_sdk has no workspace trust option.

upstream.behavior: An accepted trust needs a directory that is absolute on posix or win32; otherwise the whole value is dropped with a warning. A declined or empty trust passes through as given.

rows.concept: Marking user messages client_composed so the CLI skips @path expansion and slash commands

upstream.behavior: With the option on, every outgoing user message carries client_composed:true after its other keys. Python additionally warns at the first init message when the CLI is older than 2.1.248 or reports no version.

rows.concept: error_code on a control error response

upstream.behavior: TypeScript keeps a string error_code matching /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$/ as errorCode and drops any other; Python raises with the message only.

decision.reason: ControlRejectionError::error_code reads it the TypeScript way by default; ArgvStyle::Python leaves it unset like Python.

rows.concept: Control responses returned to the caller

upstream.behavior: Neither SDK validates a control response. TypeScript returns the response as sent, undefined when absent; Python returns it when it is an object and an empty object otherwise.

decision.reason: ControlReply keeps the response as sent, None when absent, and decodes it to the pinned type only on request; ArgvStyle::Python reads a missing or non-object response as an empty object.

rows.concept: set_model without a model

upstream.behavior: TypeScript setModel() leaves model out of the request; Python set_model(None) sends model null.

decision.reason: set_model(None) leaves model out by default and sends null under ArgvStyle::Python.

rows.concept: rewind_files dry run flag

upstream.behavior: TypeScript sends dry_run as the caller's dryRun, left out when unset; Python sends only user_message_id.

decision.reason: rewind_files(id, None) sends what both SDKs send without the option; RewindMode::DryRun and RewindMode::Apply send the TypeScript flag.

rows.concept: Slash commands after commands_changed, and the getters over the initialization result

python.reason: The pinned Python client has no supported commands accessor.

upstream.behavior: supportedCommands destructures the initialization result first, then returns the commands of the last system commands_changed message whose commands is an array, else the initialize commands. supportedModels, supportedAgents and accountInfo read their field off the initialization result. rows.concept: The can_use_tool answer built from the callback result

decision.reason: AnsweredOutOfBand writes nothing by default; ArgvStyle::Python answers a permission request with Python's TypeError text.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript aborts the callback's signal and still writes whatever the callback then returns. Python cancels the handler task, so no response is written.

decision.reason: The callback's signal is cancelled and its answer is still written by default; ArgvStyle::Python aborts the task without a response.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript answers an unknown subtype with error_code unsupported_request, declines an elicitation without a handler, leaves dialogs and the remote tool subtypes unanswered, and names the missing getOAuthToken, getHostAuthToken or refreshWorkSecret callback. Python handles only can_use_tool, hook_callback and mcp_message and answers everything else with its unsupported-subtype error and no error_code.

python.reason: The pinned Python transport closes the process its own way.

rows.concept: Home directory when HOME is unset or empty

upstream.behavior: Neither SDK fails for a missing HOME. TypeScript calls Node os.homedir(): HOME as set (even empty), else the passwd entry of the effective user, and it throws a system error only when there is no entry; the result is joined with path.join, which normalizes dot segments, repeated separators and empty bases. Python calls Path.home() (expanduser): HOME as set (even empty, which becomes the root directory), else the passwd entry of the real user, else it raises RuntimeError; a home that still starts with a tilde also raises, and dot-dot segments are kept. Both read the process environment, not options.env. Rust ports the exact algorithms: Node path.win32.join and normalize over UTF-16 code units, CPython ntpath.expanduser, splitroot and join with the pathlib PureWindowsPath normalization, byte-exact POSIX homes that are not UTF-8 (lossy UTF-8 for Node, surrogate escapes for Python), and the Windows process-token profile directory that libuv asks. Python has no Windows passwd fallback. The Python dialect reports a missing home as the RuntimeError text through SessionFiles::from_environment and the session helpers instead of an empty result.

rows.concept: Closing a query while control requests wait for their answers

upstream.behavior: TypeScript's close is idempotent: it aborts in-flight callbacks, closes the transport, rejects every control and MCP request still waiting with Query closed before response received, and ends the message stream cleanly. Python's close cancels the read task without failing waiting control requests, so each one runs out its own timeout with Control request timeout: <subtype>, and the buffered messages stay readable.

decision.reason: close() on a Query, the client or a handle takes &self, so it can be called while the stream is read, and rejects waiting control requests with Error::QueryClosed by default while the messages already received stay readable before the stream ends; ArgvStyle::Python leaves each to its control timeout as Python does. disconnect(self) on the query or the client closes and waits for the process in both styles.

rows.concept: A caller-supplied abort controller stops the process

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no abort controller; cancellation is the caller's task cancellation.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript listens on abortController (a fresh one by default): aborting it closes the process, an already aborted controller closes it at spawn, an exit while aborted is Claude Code process aborted by user, and a write after it is Operation aborted. Closing the query does not abort the caller's controller.

rows.concept: A caller-supplied spawn function starts the CLI

python.reason: The pinned Python sources spawn the CLI only through their own subprocess transport; a custom peer is a Transport.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript hands spawnClaudeCodeProcess the command, arguments, working directory, the whole child environment and its forwarded abort signal, uses the process it returns in place of its own spawn, derives no default debug file for it, and aborts the forwarded signal only after the close grace when the caller's controller was aborted.

rows.concept: The SDK reports the process it spawned

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no spawn callback.

upstream.behavior: After its own spawn, TypeScript calls onProcessSpawned with the pid and the milliseconds the spawn call took, only when the pid is known, and logs and ignores a throw from it.

rows.concept: The host answers a remote control work secret refresh

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no work secret answerer; they answer the request with their unsupported subtype error.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript answers remote_control_work_secret only for the session the last enableRemoteControl attached, comparing ids with j8 (equal, or the same suffix of at least four characters after the last underscore). A missing answerer, or a session this host did not attach, is an error; otherwise refreshWorkSecret runs with the attached session id and the signal and an empty result answers {work_secret:null}.

rows.concept: enableRemoteControl installs the work secret answerer

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no enableRemoteControl method; they answer the request with their unsupported subtype error.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript sends remote_control with the optional name, reattach_session_id, keep_session_on_exit and work_secret. When enabling and still the latest call, a response that is absent or null throws the engine TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (or null) (reading 'bridge_session_id') after the answerer was installed, so the answerer stays; when disabling, the response is returned as it is. It answers for reattachSessionId, else the session id inside the work secret's ingress token, only when enabling with a work secret and a refresh function. A failed call clears the answerer unless a newer call began, and a successful enable keeps the candidate that j8 matches to the response's bridge_session_id.

rows.concept: A uiHost draws the CLI's prompt

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no uiHost option; they answer the request with their unsupported subtype error.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript routes ui_copy, ui_prompt_read, ui_prompt_fill, ui_prompt_paint, ui_prompt_suggest and ui_read_selection to the matching uiHost method with the request minus its subtype and the signal; the method's return value is the response, and an undefined return answers success without a response key. A subtype whose method is absent falls through to the unsupported request error.

rows.concept: The run ends at its result only when nothing needs the CLI to keep asking, and the reader keeps yielding until the CLI exits

upstream.behavior: TypeScript treats a run as needing the CLI when it has an embedded MCP server, a non-empty hooks object, canUseTool, onElicitation, onUserDialog, getOAuthToken, getHostAuthToken or a work secret answerer. Python's _has_bidirectional_needs knows only SDK MCP servers, hooks and can_use_tool. A streamed input is closed as soon as it was written when nothing needs the CLI, in both. A prompt string is a single user turn in TypeScript: a result ends it, and closes stdin, when the session reported no state or is idle or when nothing needs the CLI, otherwise the run end waits for idle or its ceiling. Python closes stdin as soon as a prompt string was written when nothing needs the CLI, and otherwise waits for the run to end. Both readers keep yielding every message the CLI sends after the result until the CLI exits.

rows.concept: Stdin closes by the run-end machine of each upstream SDK: results, session state, the ceiling and, in Python, tracked agents, with nothing else moving the moment

upstream.behavior: TypeScript: a written prompt clears the result and ends nothing; a result ends the run when the session reported no state or is idle or when nothing needs the CLI, and otherwise arms the ceiling; idle after a result ends it; any other state reopens it and restarts or clears the ceiling (requires_action clears); main-thread assistant or stream frames reopen it and clear the ceiling; ending a single user turn closes stdin and a streamed input waits for the end only when it wrote a prompt and something needs the CLI. Tasks and queued turns play no part. Python adds tracked local_agent and local_workflow tasks: while one is in flight a result or idle does not end the run and the ceiling leaves it alone, and the ceiling restarts once the last one settles; it also never arms the ceiling during a main-thread turn or without needs.

rows.concept: Under the TypeScript style connect returns once the initialize request is queued, and a control request issued then is written right behind it

upstream.behavior: TypeScript request() writes at once when the initialize request is already written or being written, so enableRemoteControl called before initialize resolves lands on the wire after the initialize bytes and before the initialize response is read. The TypeScript style of connect and query returns as soon as the initialize request is queued, so the same bytes land at the same point by default. Python awaits start and initialize inside connect, so the Python style returns only after the initialize response.

rows.concept: An initialize failure surfaces through the stream and getters, and prompts wait behind initialize when blocking hooks or managed settings are set

python.reason: The pinned Python sources wait for the initialize response inside connect, so a failure is raised by connect and no prompt can be written earlier.

upstream.behavior: TypeScript holds prompts, interrupts and settings-bearing controls behind the initialization promise and releases them in order once it resolves. A rejection, or the 660 second timer that fires when initialize never answers, cleans the query up: nothing held is written, every held and pending request is rejected with the initialize error, and the stream ends with it. Rust holds the same commands in the driver under the TypeScript style when blocking hooks or managed settings are set, releases them in order on success, rejects them with the initialize error on failure or timeout, and reports the failure through the stream and the async initialization getters as InitializationFailed. The goldens were captured from sdk.mjs for the success, error and timer paths.

rows.concept: How a streamed input stops, fails and closes stdin

upstream.behavior: Both write each streamed message in order and close stdin once the stream ends, waiting for the run to end first only when that call wrote something and, in TypeScript, something needs the CLI; each counts the prompts of its own call, so one that wrote nothing closes stdin at once. TypeScript stops at an abort and resolves, stops once a failed prompt hold cleaned the query up, writes behind a pending prompt hold and skips closing stdin when the hold resolves false, and rejects with the write error after close or with the stream's own error while leaving stdin open. Python stops once the query is closed, logs a stream or write failure and closes stdin anyway, and never raises.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect; ArgvStyle::Python reproduces the Python stream_input, and try_stream_input carries a fallible stream so both failure paths are reachable.

rows.concept: Session id written on a prompt that names none

upstream.behavior: Python ClaudeSDKClient.query and connect(str) write a string prompt in session "default" unless query names another, and query(AsyncIterable) sets that session only on messages without a session_id key. sdk.mjs writes a string prompt with an empty session_id and passes an AsyncIterable prompt through unchanged.

decision.reason: TypeScript is the default dialect, so ClaudeSdkClient::query writes the empty session. Under ArgvStyle::Python it writes "default", and query_in_session, query_stream and query_stream_in_session follow Python's query(prompt, session_id).

rows.concept: How long startup() waits for the CLI to answer initialize

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no pre-warming.

upstream.behavior: startup() races the initialize answer against a timer. Without initializeTimeoutMs it allows 60000 ms and does not count the time in which Claude Code reports a SessionStart or Setup hook running, for at most 600000 ms; a value the caller passes counts throughout. The error names the limit, the uncounted seconds and what the reported hooks did, and carries the errorClass initialize_timeout with its first sentence as telemetryMessage. The default 60000 ms run and its uncounted hook seconds were captured live with a node harness that sent the hook frames at fixed offsets and never answered initialize. The ten minute cap was captured the same way: a Setup hook open from 20 seconds on made the timeout fire at 660 seconds and report 600 uncounted seconds.

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no pre-warming.

Only marks of at most 64 characters count, and hook progress frames are dropped while the wait lasts. The expected texts were captured live from sdk.mjs 0.3.323 driven by a scripted CLI.

rows.concept: Why an error result exit names a startup failure

python.reason: The pinned Python sources have no pre-warming.

typescript.anchor: Claude Code returned an error result: ${t}`),{telemetryMessage:"Claude Code returned an error result",errorClass:"error_result",startupFailureReason:this.lastStartupFailureReason}

upstream.behavior: The error that replaces a failed exit carries startupFailureReason, the startup_failure_reason of the last error result when it is a string, so a host can tell a refusal to start from any other failure. The error text is the result text of a success subtype or the trimmed, non-empty errors joined by a semicolon and a space.
